candidates.title: Show HN: How do you know your LLM giving accurate info?
candidates.raw_content: I spend a good amount of time chasing the LLM for evidence that its answer is actually accurate. To be honest, I can usually get there, but it works great for fresh work and gets messy on months-old work. And it's not just me; a lot of people have raised the same thing. So for the last 6 months I've been trying to fix it. Today I can say it's working for me — it flags me in advance. Obviously not perfect yet, and that's where I need help: I need people to test it and tell me what else needs fixing. PS: This isn't a memory layer; it flags stale answers before you act on them. Give it a try, and if you think I'm solving a real problem, please drop a star. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49624134 Points: 1 # Comments: 1

candidates.title: I am pleased to see that Ant’s new Claude Code has a version of background computer use on par with the version from Codex from last May this year. Nice work! Shipping great features first turns out to be a great way to encourage other labs to ship too. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to shipping. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go! We solved computer use in practice for GPT models about four months ago. But computer use is a significantly awesome thing no matter what model you use, and it is important that the industry similarly spends more effort to train their models to be great at computer use, among other elements of model capabilities. As models become more capable and central to businesses and economies, the value of computer use only increases. We should be taking it seriously, and doing the right thing for our customers and the world.

candidates.title: It's a weird time. As many of you know, my superpower is optimism. I have an insane ability to look at any situation through the most positive lens. I strongly believe that today is the "least best" (not worst) day of my life and tomorrow will be glorious. I am super optimistic about where AI is going. But I also find myself genuinely anxious about the pace of change and our inability to understand how these (insanely) complicated machines work. I always err on the side of "just let us cook". The only way out is through. Let us build. But man, it is a weird time.

candidates.title: This kind of tweet is both interesting and misleading. On the one hand, who doesn’t want a personalized vaccine that treats their cancer and reduces the need for chemo? On the other hand, there are many patients and families desperately looking for treatment. Presenting this as what cancer treatment looks like in 2026 is just not true: 1. Promising results in melanoma don’t mean personalized vaccines work across all cancers. 2. A treatment showing promise in a trial doesn’t mean most patients can get it or benefit from it. I’d love to hear from oncologists like @RoupenMD @jasonwilliamsmd: 1. How close are we to making personalized cancer vaccines a realistic option for most patients? 2. What’s still standing in the way?
